title: Allow to position status line on the top
body:
When I want to duplicate a buffer I cannot see the path of the current buffer anymore:

I see the path of the current buffer in the status line

![Screenshot at Feb 01 08-36-58](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1005498/215889744-0618dee4-9470-4768-8597-927d41e14339.png)

Then when I type `:w` I cannot see the path of the buffer anymore as it is obscured by the popup.

![Screenshot at Feb 01 08-37-43](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1005498/215889882-01741c6f-4b07-4065-8951-0b635e36bfde.png)

I would like to keep the path of the buffer visible, so I can copy part of the path.

So having an option to position the status line at the top would be great for this. So it is always visible.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> I would like to keep the path of the buffer visible, so I can copy part of the path.

If your goal is to copy/paste the path up to the parent directory, #3134 *might* help you once implemented. However there hasn't been much development on this issue in a while.

> so, would u still consider this solved or is only the proposed solution your focus??

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
Hi. While trying to do this I thought that it is actually not ideal.

If you have the prompt with the suggestions, the bar will look weird when it overflows over the popup and it would also move a lot, which I think makes it harder to use. So I came up with the idea to actually put the statusline under the prompt. The statusline would stay static and will be easy to see and you also don't get distracted by the suggestions. That is at least what I think would be the best option.

Would you also consider this?

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/76444201/217391424-86936eee-597b-470e-9544-27994388589b.png)

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
- i dont _think_ it will make sense for it to be configurable
- the new placement better be hard coded as is the current placement.... 
- status above cmdline works in vim due to its lack of feedback, and hence, increases the contrast between the buffer text and cmdline...

But having popups, that's not the case with helix now, so, i can see no reason for keeping status line above (if there is, please share 😃).
- just a small ghost line can be added to increase separation if wanted by team
- but i can see ppl wanting to customise every bit without _any specific reason_ which i aint a fan of.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: oh and also, in ur screenshot, one more suggestion is to make the line above (i.e commandline) to switch colors with line below (status line) so that position wise colors stay same as current situation - this will ensure the contrast.
